item.title: Kafka Topic as a Service: Automating GitOps Workflows with Kestra and Jikkou
item.description:
Photo by Barrington Ratliff on Unsplash

This blog post was originally published on Medium

From manual CLI commands to a fully automated, human-in-the-loop provisioning service with Kestra and Jikkou on Aiven’s free Kafka tier.

Managing Apache Kafka resources at scale is one of those problems that starts simple and quickly becomes painful. One day you’re running kafka-topic.sh from your terminal, and the next you’re the gatekeeper for dozens of teams who all need topics, ACLs, and connectors, and of course they needed them yesterday.

item.title: Kafka Connect + Jikkou: Easily manage Kafka connectors
item.description:
Photo by Miltiadis Fragkidis on Unsplash

This blog post was originally published on Medium

Kafka Connect is a widely used solution to stream data into Apache Kafka and to transfer data from Kafka to external systems for further use, such as online analytical processing.

One of the main advantages of Kafka Connect is its ease of use. Basically, all you have to do is define the JSON configuration corresponding to the connector you want to run and push it to the REST API of your Kafka Connect cluster to start data integration.

item.title: GitOps & Kafka: Enabling smooth and seamless Data Schema management with Jikkou and GitHub Actions
item.description:
This blog post was originally published on Medium

Photo by Vighnesh Dudani on Unsplash

Data schemas are a fundamental part of the definition and documentation of the event streams in an event-driven platform such as Apache Kafka . Not only do schemas provide a clear definition of the field names, types, and defaults of the content of the data, but they also serve as a way to standardize data contracts between both producers and consumers.

item.title: Jikkou: Declarative ACLs configuration for Apache Kafka and Schema Registry on Aiven
item.description:
Photo by iMattSmart on Unsplash

Whether you’ve been running Apache Kafka in production for a few days or a while, you should be aware that creating and managing topics, Access Control, Schemas, etc. by hand is tedious and error-prone.

A better approach is to rely on declarative configuration, revision control and automation to build repeatable and traceable workflows for managing the things of your data streaming platform. In other words, GitOps-style is the way!

item.title: Why is Managing Kafka Topics Still Such a Pain? Introducing Jikkou!
item.description:
Photo by Jon Cartagena on Unsplash

#Motivation

Since I started working with Apache Kafka eight years ago, managing topics on a scalable platform has always been a headache for both developers and infrastructure teams. Of course, when a Kafka cluster is used and managed by a single team, creating and managing topics remains relatively simple. In such cases, using Kafka CLI kafka-topics.sh and kafka-configs.sh may be sufficient to meet daily operational needs.

item.title: How to build a real-time analytics platform using Kafka, ksqlDB and ClickHouse ?
item.description:
Apache Kafka + ksqlDB + ClickHouse + Superset = Blazing Fast Analytics Platform

This blog post was originally published on Medium

Recently at StreamThoughts, we have looked at different open-source OLAP databases that we could quickly experiment in a streaming architecture, based on the Apache Kafka platform.

Our goal was to be able to respond to analytical needs on large volumes of data that were ingested in real-time. For this, we were looking for a solution that would allow us to execute ad-hoc queries, interactively, with “acceptable” latencies (a few seconds or more).

item.title: Kafka Connect FilePulse - One Connector to Ingest them All!
item.description:
Photo by Brandon Green on Unsplash

This blog post was originally published on Medium

Most of the projects I’ve worked on in the last few years have involved ingesting data into systems such as Apache Kafka® and Apache Hadoop® to perform processing and data enrichment both in real-time and in batch.

One of the recurring challenges of each of these projects has always been to manage the complexity of legacy systems in which data was frequently exported, shared and integrated through the use of files.

item.title: Understanding Kafka partition assignment strategies and how to write your own custom assignor
item.description:
This blog post was originally published on Medium

In a previous blog post , I explain how the Apache Kafka Rebalance Protocol does work and how is internally used. From the point of view of Kafka consumers, this protocol is leveraged both to coordinate members belonging to the same group and to distribute topic-partition ownership amongst them.

One of the key aspect of this protocol is that, as a developer, we can embed our own protocol to customize how partitions are assigned to the group members.

item.title: Apache Kafka Rebalance Protocol, or the magic behind your streams applications
item.description:
This blog post was originally published on Medium

Since Apache Kafka 2.3.0, the internal Rebalance Protocol, which is especially used by Kafka Connect and consumers, has undergone several major changes.

The Rebalance Protocol is not something simple and can sometimes look like magic. In this post, I propose to go back to the foundation of this protocol, which is at the heart of the Apache Kafka consumption mechanism. Then, we will discuss its limitations and current improvements.
